subproblem.title: Assembling componentwise affine approximations into a vector affine map
subproblem.statement: Let n, k ∈ ℕ, f : ℝⁿ → ℝᵏ continuous, s > 0 and A, B, Q, t ∈ ℝ. Suppose that for every j ∈ Fin k there are a ∈ ℝ and a continuous linear functional b on ℝⁿ with ‖b‖ ≤ B, |a| ≤ A and ∫_{B̆ⁿ_t(0)} (s⁻¹fʲ(v) − a − b(v))² dv ≤ Q (Bochner integral over the open ball; fʲ := EuclideanSpace.proj j ∘ f). Then there are c ∈ ℝᵏ and a continuous linear Λ : ℝⁿ → ℝᵏ with |c| ≤ k·s·A, ‖Λ‖ ≤ k·s·B and ∫_{B̆ⁿ_t(0)} |f(v) − c − Λv|² dv ≤ k·s²·Q, the last as the lower integral of ENNReal.ofReal bounded by ENNReal.ofReal(k s² Q).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n k : ℕ) (f : Euclid n → Euclid k) (s A B Q t : ℝ), Continuous f → 0 < s → (∀ j : Fin k, ∃ (a : ℝ) (b : Euclid n →L[ℝ] ℝ), ‖b‖ ≤ B ∧ |a| ≤ A ∧ ∫ v in ball (0 : Euclid n) t, (s⁻¹ * EuclideanSpace.proj j (f v) - a - b v) ^ 2 ≤ Q) → ∃ (c : Euclid k) (Λ : Euclid n →L[ℝ] Euclid k), ‖c‖ ≤ k * s * A ∧ ‖Λ‖ ≤ k * s * B ∧ ∫⁻ v in ball (0 : Euclid n) t, ENNReal.ofReal (‖f v - c - Λ v‖ ^ 2) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (k * s ^ 2 * Q)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof Steps 7–8 (Simon Ch. 5, proof of 4.5, (17)–(19)): λʲ(v) = (C₁₃E₀)^{1/2}(a_j + b_j(v)), u(0) = λ(0), Du(0) = Dλ, and summing the componentwise L² bounds over j. The parent applies it with s := (C₁₃E₀)^{1/2}, t := θ′R₀, B := C_H, A := C_H(s⁻¹ω_n^{1/2}C₇δ^ασ + ε′^{1/2}R₀) and Q := C_H(ε′/θ′^{n+2} + θ′²)(θ′R₀)^{n+2}, the a_j, b_j coming from harmonic_approximation applied to w = s⁻¹fʲ.
1. If k = 0, take c := 0 and Λ := 0. Then |c| = 0 = k s A and ‖Λ‖ = 0 = k s B, and since ℝ⁰ = {0}, |f(v) − c − Λv| = 0, so the lower integral is 0 ≤ ofReal(0). Assume k ≥ 1 from now on.
2. For each j choose (a_j, b_j) as in the hypothesis (choice over the finite set Fin k). Then A ≥ |a_0| ≥ 0, B ≥ ‖b_0‖ ≥ 0, and Q ≥ ∫(…)² ≥ 0 because a Bochner integral of a nonnegative function is nonnegative.
3. Define c := Σ_j s a_j ε_j ∈ ℝᵏ and Λv := Σ_j s b_j(v) ε_j, where ε_j := EuclideanSpace.single j 1 (Lean: Λ := Σ_j (s • b_j).smulRight ε_j). Then Λ is continuous linear, proj_j(c) = s a_j and proj_j(Λv) = s b_j(v).
4. Norms. |c| ≤ Σ_j |s a_j||ε_j| ≤ k s A by the triangle inequality and s > 0. For every v, |Λv| ≤ Σ_j s|b_j(v)| ≤ k s B|v|, so ‖Λ‖ ≤ k s B (ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_le_bound, k s B ≥ 0).
5. Pointwise identity. For every v, |f(v) − c − Λv|² = Σ_j (proj_j f(v) − s a_j − s b_j(v))² = Σ_j s²(s⁻¹proj_j f(v) − a_j − b_j(v))², using the Euclidean norm on ℝᵏ (EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq) and s ≠ 0.
6. Integrability. Each v ↦ (s⁻¹proj_j f(v) − a_j − b_j(v))² is continuous, because f and b_j are. The open ball B̆ⁿ_t(0) is bounded with compact closure and finite Lebesgue measure, so each such function is bounded on it and integrable there (for t ≤ 0 the ball is empty and all integrals vanish). By step 5 and linearity, ∫_{B̆_t}|f − c − Λ·|² dv = Σ_j s²∫_{B̆_t}(s⁻¹fʲ − a_j − b_j)² dv ≤ k s² Q.
7. Lower integral. v ↦ |f(v) − c − Λv|² is nonnegative and integrable on B̆_t, so ∫⁻_{B̆_t} ofReal(|f − c − Λ·|²) = ofReal(∫_{B̆_t}|f − c − Λ·|²) (ofReal_integral_eq_lintegral_ofReal) ≤ ofReal(k s² Q). ∎
proof_key_steps: Handle k = 0 with c = 0, Λ = 0.
Choose (a_j, b_j) for each j and set c := Σ_j s a_j ε_j and Λ := Σ_j (s b_j)(·)ε_j.
Triangle inequality: |c| ≤ k s A and ‖Λ‖ ≤ k s B.
|f − c − Λ·|² = Σ_j s²(s⁻¹fʲ − a_j − b_j)²; each term is continuous, hence integrable on the ball; sum the L² bounds and pass to the lower integral.

subproblem.title: Area bounds for a 1-Lipschitz graph over an n-plane
subproblem.statement: Let n ≥ 1, k ≥ 0, ι : ℝⁿ → ℝ^{n+k} and ι' : ℝᵏ → ℝ^{n+k} linear isometries with ⟨ιv, ι'w⟩ = 0 for all v, w, ξ ∈ ℝ^{n+k}, f : ℝⁿ → ℝᵏ with |f(v) − f(w)| ≤ |v − w| for all v, w, and Φ(v) := ξ + ιv + ι'f(v). Then for every measurable set A ⊆ ℝⁿ and every measurable h : ℝ^{n+k} → [0, ∞]: ∫_A h(Φ(v)) dLⁿ(v) ≤ ∫_{Φ(A)} h dHⁿ ≤ ∫_A (1 + 2ⁿ Σ_{i=1}^{n} |Df(v)e_i|²) h(Φ(v)) dLⁿ(v). Here Hⁿ = μHE[n] on ℝ^{n+k}, Lⁿ = volume on ℝⁿ, Df(v) = fderiv ℝ f v (0 where f is not differentiable), e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1, the weight is ENNReal.ofReal of the displayed real number, and all integrals are lower Lebesgue integrals.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n k : ℕ), 0 < n → ∀ (ι : Euclid n →ₗᵢ[ℝ] Euclid (n + k)) (ι' : Euclid k →ₗᵢ[ℝ] Euclid (n + k)) (ξ : Euclid (n + k)) (f : Euclid n → Euclid k) (A : Set (Euclid n)) (h : Euclid (n + k) → ℝ≥0∞), (∀ v w, inner ℝ (ι v) (ι' w) = 0) → (∀ v w, ‖f v - f w‖ ≤ ‖v - w‖) → MeasurableSet A → Measurable h → (∫⁻ v in A, h (ξ + ι v + ι' (f v)) ≤ ∫⁻ x in (fun v => ξ + ι v + ι' (f v)) '' A, h x ∂μHE[n]) ∧ ∫⁻ x in (fun v => ξ + ι v + ι' (f v)) '' A, h x ∂μHE[n] ≤ ∫⁻ v in A, ENNReal.ofReal (1 + 2 ^ n * ∑ i : Fin n, ‖fderiv ℝ f v (EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ))‖ ^ 2) * h (ξ + ι v + ι' (f v))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof Step 6 (area formula for the injective Lipschitz graph map, J_f ∈ [1, 2^{n/2}], |J_f − 1| ≤ C|Df|²) and Step 9 (J_f ≤ 2^{n/2}); Simon Ch. 5, (14)–(15), and the area formula Simon Ch. 2, 3.5. Write J_Φ(v) := (det(DΦ(v)^*DΦ(v)))^{1/2} where Φ is differentiable at v, J_Φ(v) := 0 otherwise (Lean: areaJacobianAt Φ v = (fderiv ℝ Φ v).normDet).
1. Φ is injective. If Φ(v) = Φ(w) then ι(v − w) = ι'(f(w) − f(v)); taking the inner product with ι(v − w), and using that ι is an isometry and ⟨ιu, ι'u'⟩ = 0, gives |v − w|² = |ι(v − w)|² = ⟨ι(v − w), ι'(f(w) − f(v))⟩ = 0, so v = w.
2. Φ is 2-Lipschitz: |Φ(v) − Φ(w)| ≤ |ι(v − w)| + |ι'(f(v) − f(w))| = |v − w| + |f(v) − f(w)| ≤ 2|v − w|.
3. Area formula. For an injective Lipschitz map Φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^{n+k}, a measurable A ⊆ ℝⁿ and any g : ℝ^{n+k} → [0, ∞], ∫_{Φ(A)} g dHⁿ = ∫_A J_Φ(v) g(Φ(v)) dLⁿ(v) (Simon Ch. 2, 3.5–3.7; Federer 3.2.3). It is proved, with axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound only, in the pinned SimonGMT package as Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.weighted_area_formula_lipschitz_injOn (file Poincare/SimonGMT/Chapter02/AreaLipschitz.lean; add `import Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.AreaLipschitz` to the import block of GMT/Ch07/Submission.lean — adding a SimonGMT import has precedent in the accepted node root.density_and_tangent_cones-a1.im_sub-a1, commit 77fcc7d). Its measure is μHE[finrank ℝ (Euclid n)] = μHE[n] (finrank_euclideanSpace_fin), and its Jacobian is areaJacobianAt Φ v, whose square is det(DΦ(v)^*DΦ(v)) (areaJacobianAt_sq_eq_det_adjoint_comp).
4. Differentiability. By Rademacher's theorem (LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt) f is differentiable at Lⁿ-a.e. v. Fix such a v and put B := Df(v) : ℝⁿ → ℝᵏ. Since f is 1-Lipschitz, ‖B‖ ≤ 1 (norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz), so |Be_i| ≤ 1 for every i. Φ is differentiable at v with DΦ(v) = ι + ι'∘B.
5. Gram operator. For u, w ∈ ℝⁿ, ⟨DΦ(v)u, DΦ(v)w⟩ = ⟨ιu, ιw⟩ + ⟨ιu, ι'Bw⟩ + ⟨ι'Bu, ιw⟩ + ⟨ι'Bu, ι'Bw⟩ = ⟨u, w⟩ + ⟨Bu, Bw⟩. The two middle terms vanish by orthogonality, and ι, ι' preserve inner products. Hence DΦ(v)^*DΦ(v) = I + P with P := B^*B.
6. Spectrum. P is self-adjoint with 0 ≤ ⟨Pu, u⟩ = |Bu|² ≤ |u|². By the spectral theorem P has an orthonormal eigenbasis with eigenvalues λ_1, …, λ_n ∈ [0, 1], and Σ_iλ_i = trace P = Σ_i⟨Pe_i, e_i⟩ = Σ_i|Be_i|² =: t(v).
7. Determinant. det(I + P) = Π_i(1 + λ_i) ≥ 1. Claim: for m ≥ 1 and λ_1, …, λ_m ∈ [0, 1], Π_{i≤m}(1 + λ_i) ≤ 1 + 2^{m−1}S_m with S_m := Σ_{i≤m}λ_i. For m = 1 this is an equality. If it holds for m, then Π_{i≤m+1}(1 + λ_i) ≤ (1 + λ_{m+1})(1 + 2^{m−1}S_m) = 1 + 2^{m−1}S_m + λ_{m+1} + λ_{m+1}2^{m−1}S_m ≤ 1 + 2^mS_m + λ_{m+1} ≤ 1 + 2^mS_{m+1}, using λ_{m+1} ≤ 1 and 1 ≤ 2^m. With m = n ≥ 1: 1 ≤ J_Φ(v)² = det(I + P) ≤ 1 + 2^{n−1}t(v).
8. Since J_Φ(v) ≥ 0 and J_Φ(v)² ≥ 1, we get J_Φ(v) ≥ 1, hence J_Φ(v) ≤ J_Φ(v)² ≤ 1 + 2^{n−1}t(v) ≤ 1 + 2ⁿΣ_i|Df(v)e_i|². So 1 ≤ J_Φ(v) ≤ 1 + 2ⁿΣ_i|Df(v)e_i|² for Lⁿ-a.e. v.
9. Integration. Multiply the a.e. inequalities of step 8 (read in [0, ∞] through ENNReal.ofReal) by h(Φ(v)) ∈ [0, ∞]. Integrate over A, using monotonicity of the lower integral under a.e. inequalities for the restricted measure (lintegral_mono_ae), and use step 3 with g := h. This gives ∫_A h(Φ(v)) dv ≤ ∫_A J_Φ(v)h(Φ(v)) dv = ∫_{Φ(A)} h dHⁿ ≤ ∫_A ofReal(1 + 2ⁿΣ_i|Df(v)e_i|²) h(Φ(v)) dv, which is the claim. ∎
proof_key_steps: Φ(v) = ξ + ιv + ι'f(v) is injective and 2-Lipschitz.
Area formula for injective Lipschitz maps (SimonGMT weighted_area_formula_lipschitz_injOn): ∫_{Φ(A)} h dHⁿ = ∫_A J_Φ h∘Φ dv.
Rademacher: a.e. DΦ = ι + ι'Df with ‖Df‖ ≤ 1, and DΦ^*DΦ = I + Df^*Df.

subproblem.title: Hilbert–Schmidt inequalities for orthogonal projections
subproblem.statement: Let N ∈ ℕ, V := ℝ^N (Lean Euclid N) with standard orthonormal basis e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1, and for a subspace Q ⊆ V let p_Q := Q.starProjection be the orthogonal projection onto Q. For a continuous linear A : V → V put |A|² := Σ_i |Ae_i|², and for subspaces Q, T write |p_Q − p_T|² := Σ_i |p_Qe_i − p_Te_i|². Then: (a) |Ay|² ≤ |A|²|y|² for every continuous linear A : V → V and every y ∈ V; (b) |p_S − p_T|² ≤ 2|p_Q − p_S|² + 2|p_Q − p_T|² for all subspaces Q, S, T; (c) |⟨p_Qa, b⟩ − ⟨a, b⟩| ≤ |p_Q − p_T|²|a||b| for all subspaces Q, T and all a, b ∈ T; (d) |p_Qe|² ≤ |p_Q − p_T|²|e|² for all subspaces Q, T and every e ∈ T^⊥.

Source: parent proof Step 1 (|p_T − p_{T̃}|² ≤ 2|p_x − p_T|² + 2|p_x − p_{T̃}|² and dist(x − ξ, T) ≤ dist(x − ξ, T̃) + ‖p_T − p_{T̃}‖|x − ξ|), Step 4 (|p_xe_{n+j}| = |(p_x − p_T)e_{n+j}| ≤ |p_x − p_T|) and Step 5 (identity (11): p_Tp_x^⊥p_T = (p_T − p_x)p_x^⊥(p_T − p_x)); Simon Ch. 5, 4.4 and (10)–(11). Notation: for a continuous linear A put |A| := (Σ_i|Ae_i|²)^{1/2} ≥ 0.
1. Proof of (a). Let y ∈ V and y_i := ⟨y, e_i⟩. Since (e_i) is an orthonormal basis, y = Σ_i y_ie_i and Σ_i y_i² = |y|². By linearity Ay = Σ_i y_iAe_i. By the triangle inequality and the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality for finite sums, |Ay| ≤ Σ_i|y_i||Ae_i| ≤ (Σ_iy_i²)^{1/2}(Σ_i|Ae_i|²)^{1/2} = |y||A|. Both sides are nonnegative, so squaring gives |Ay|² ≤ |A|²|y|². We also record (a′): |Ay| ≤ |A||y|.
2. Proof of (b). Fix i and put u := p_Qe_i − p_Se_i and w := p_Qe_i − p_Te_i. Then p_Se_i − p_Te_i = w − u, and by the parallelogram law |w − u|² ≤ |w − u|² + |w + u|² = 2|w|² + 2|u|². Summing over i gives Σ_i|p_Se_i − p_Te_i|² ≤ 2Σ_i|p_Qe_i − p_Se_i|² + 2Σ_i|p_Qe_i − p_Te_i|².
3. Facts used below. Let B := p_Q − p_T (continuous linear). Then Be_i = p_Qe_i − p_Te_i, so |B|² = |p_Q − p_T|². For every y the vector y − p_Qy lies in Q^⊥ and p_Qy ∈ Q; p_T fixes every vector of T and annihilates every vector of T^⊥.
4. Proof of (c). Let a, b ∈ T. Since a − p_Qa ∈ Q^⊥ and p_Qb ∈ Q, ⟨a − p_Qa, p_Qb⟩ = 0, hence ⟨a − p_Qa, b⟩ = ⟨a − p_Qa, b − p_Qb⟩. Because p_Ta = a and p_Tb = b we have a − p_Qa = p_Ta − p_Qa = −Ba and b − p_Qb = −Bb. Therefore ⟨p_Qa, b⟩ − ⟨a, b⟩ = −⟨a − p_Qa, b⟩ = −⟨Ba, Bb⟩, and by Cauchy–Schwarz and (a′), |⟨p_Qa, b⟩ − ⟨a, b⟩| ≤ |Ba||Bb| ≤ (|B||a|)(|B||b|) = |p_Q − p_T|²|a||b|.
5. Proof of (d). Let e ∈ T^⊥. Then p_Te = 0, so p_Qe = p_Qe − p_Te = Be and, by (a), |p_Qe|² = |Be|² ≤ |B|²|e|² = |p_Q − p_T|²|e|². ∎
proof_key_steps: (a): expand y in the orthonormal basis, Ay = Σ y_iAe_i, then triangle inequality and Cauchy–Schwarz.
(b): parallelogram law |w − u|² ≤ 2|w|² + 2|u|² for each basis vector, then sum.
(c): for a, b ∈ T, ⟨p_Qa, b⟩ − ⟨a, b⟩ = −⟨a − p_Qa, b − p_Qb⟩ = −⟨(p_Q − p_T)a, (p_Q − p_T)b⟩, then Cauchy–Schwarz and (a).
(d): for e ∈ T^⊥, p_Qe = (p_Q − p_T)e, then (a).

0.1 P(Φ(v) − ξ) = P(ιv) + P(ι'f(v)) = v, i.e. φ(Φ(v)) = v; hence Φ is injective. Φ is continuous, since f is 1-Lipschitz.

It is stated here for one component j and with the domain Φ(D), D = B̆ⁿ_{r/2}. Notation: φ(x) := P(x − ξ); for g : ℝⁿ → ℝ differentiable at v, ∇g(v) ∈ ℝⁿ is its gradient (Dg(v)u = ⟨∇g(v), u⟩), so ‖Dg(v)‖ = |∇g(v)| and ∂_ig(v) = ⟨∇g(v), e_i⟩.
Step 0 (frame).
0.1 ι is injective (an isometry), so dim range ι = n = dim T. Since range ι ⊆ T, range ι = T.
0.2 V₁ := range ι and V₂ := range ι' are orthogonal, with dim V₁ = n and dim V₂ = k. Hence V₁ ∩ V₂ = 0 and dim(V₁ + V₂) = n + k, so V₁ + V₂ = ℝ^{n+k}. Since V₂ ⊆ V₁^⊥ and dim V₁^⊥ = k, V₂ = V₁^⊥ = T^⊥.
0.3 Every y ∈ ℝ^{n+k} is y = ιu + ι'w (0.2). Then Py = u, and ⟨ι^*y, u'⟩ = ⟨y, ιu'⟩ = ⟨u, u'⟩ for all u', so P = ι^* (the adjoint of ι). Consequently p_Ty = ιPy, |y|² = |Py|² + |y − p_Ty|², |Py| ≤ |y|, and for g differentiable at v: Dg(v)(Py) = ⟨∇g(v), ι^*y⟩ = ⟨ι∇g(v), y⟩.
0.4 φ(Φ(v)) = P(ιv + ι'f(v)) = v and |Φ(v) − ξ|² = |v|² + |f(v)|². For v ∈ D, |Φ(v) − ξ|² < r²/4 + r²/16 < r², so Φ(D) ⊆ B̆_r(ξ) ⊆ B_r(ξ) ⊆ W. Moreover Φ(D) = {x : x = Φ(φ(x)), φ(x) ∈ D} and F = {x : x = Φ(φ(x))} are Borel sets (Φ, φ continuous; D open).
0.5 B_r(ξ) is compact and contained in W ⊆ U, so μ(B_r(ξ)) = ∫_{M∩B_r(ξ)}θ dHⁿ < ∞ (IMRep.locallyIntegrable_mult). Also μ(ℝ^{n+k} ∖ spt μ) = 0 (complement of the support is null), and tilt_T ≤ 4(n + k) because each |p_xe_i − p_Te_i| ≤ 2.
0.6 Fix j ∈ Fin k. Let ε_j := EuclideanSpace.single j 1 ∈ ℝᵏ and e := ι'ε_j. Then |e| = 1 and e ∈ T^⊥ (0.2). fʲ is 1-Lipschitz (proj_j has norm ≤ 1), so ‖Dfʲ(v)‖ ≤ 1 for every v (norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz; Dfʲ(v) = 0 where fʲ is not differentiable).
Step 1 (graph identity (7)). Let N₀ be a μ-null set off which the tangent identification holds. Let x ∈ Φ(D) ∖ N₀ and v := φ(x), so x = Φ(v) (0.4) and x ∈ B_r(ξ). Then f is differentiable at v and T_xM = {ιw + ι'Df(v)w : w ∈ ℝⁿ}. By the chain rule Dfʲ(v) = proj_j ∘ Df(v). Put a(x) := ι∇fʲ(v) ∈ T. For w ∈ ℝⁿ, using the isometries and ⟨ιu, ι'u'⟩ = 0: ⟨ιw + ι'Df(v)w, e⟩ = ⟨Df(v)w, ε_j⟩ = Dfʲ(v)w = ⟨∇fʲ(v), w⟩ = ⟨ιw + ι'Df(v)w, a(x)⟩. Thus e − a(x) ⊥ T_xM, so (1.1) p_xe = p_xa(x). Moreover |a(x)| = |∇fʲ(v)| = ‖Dfʲ(v)‖ ≤ 1.
Step 2 (proof of (i)). Let x ∈ Φ(D) ∖ N₀ and a := a(x). By sibling proj_algebra (Submission.dorag_tes_projection_algebra), part (c), with Q := T_xM and b := a ∈ T: |a|² − ⟨p_xa, a⟩ ≤ tilt_T(x)|a|² ≤ tilt_T(x). Also ⟨p_xa, a⟩ = |p_xa|² (p_x is a self-adjoint idempotent), and |p_xa|² = |p_xe|² ≤ tilt_T(x)|e|² = tilt_T(x) by (1.1) and proj_algebra (d) (e ∈ T^⊥). 3.1 sup|ζ| ≤ Gr/2. ζ is G-Lipschitz by the mean value inequality on the convex space ℝⁿ. If |v| ≥ r/2 then v ∉ D ⊇ tsupport ζ, so ζ(v) = 0. If |v| < r/2, choose a unit vector u (u := v/|v| if v ≠ 0; any unit vector if v = 0, which exists since n ≥ 1) and put w := v + (r/2 − |v|)u. Then |w| = r/2, so ζ(w) = 0, and |ζ(v)| = |ζ(v) − ζ(w)| ≤ G|v − w| = G(r/2 − |v|) ≤ Gr/2.

3.3 Local form on spt μ. Let x ∈ spt μ ∩ B_r(ξ). If |φ(x)| < r/2, then by the height hypothesis and 0.3, |x − ξ|² = |φ(x)|² + |(x − ξ) − p_T(x − ξ)|² < r²/4 + r²/16, so |x − ξ| < (√5/4)r < 7r/8. 3.4 For x ∈ ℝ^{n+k} put b(x) := ι∇ζ(φ(x)) ∈ T. Then |b(x)| = ‖Dζ(φ(x))‖ ≤ G, and by (3.3a) and 0.3, for x ∈ spt μ ∩ B_r(ξ) and y ∈ ℝ^{n+k}: Dζ̃(x)y = Dζ(φ(x))(Py) = ⟨b(x), y⟩.

4.1 DX(x)y = (Dζ̃(x)y)e, i.e. DX(x) = (Dζ̃(x)).smulRight e. So p_x∘DX(x) = (Dζ̃(x)).smulRight(p_xe), whose trace is Dζ̃(x)(p_xe) (LinearMap.trace_smulRight). Hence tangentialDivergence n M X x = Dζ̃(x)(p_xe) for every x.
4.2 R.firstVariation X = ∫_M θ·div_M X dHⁿ by definition. This integrand is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (x ↦ p_x is, and Dζ̃ is continuous) and bounded by sup‖Dζ̃‖ < ∞. It vanishes outside B_r(ξ), which has finite measure (0.5), so it is μ-integrable. Likewise ⟨X(x), H(x)⟩ = ζ̃(x)⟨e, H(x)⟩ is integrable and |ζ̃(x)⟨e, H(x)⟩| ≤ (Gr/2)κ·1_{B_r(ξ)}(x), by 3.1, 0 ≤ h₀ ≤ 1, |e| = 1 and |H| ≤ κ.
4.3 The first-variation hypothesis applies to X (3.2), so ∫ Dζ̃(x)(p_xe) dμ = −∫ ζ̃(x)⟨e, H(x)⟩ dμ. Since both integrands vanish off B_r(ξ): |∫_{B_r(ξ)} Dζ̃(x)(p_xe) dμ| ≤ (Gr/2)κμ(B_r(ξ)).

5.1 B_r(ξ) is the disjoint union of Φ(D) and B_r(ξ) ∖ Φ(D) (0.4). For μ-a.e. x ∈ B_r(ξ), namely for x ∈ spt μ ∩ B_r(ξ), 3.4 gives Dζ̃(x)(p_xe) = ⟨b(x), p_xe⟩.

Then h₁ + (4a/M)^{1/2}σ = (2C₃ + (8C₃/ω_n)^{1/2})δ^ασ = C₁₁δ^ασ, which is (2′). Notation: B := B_σ(ξ); for a subspace S' let τ_{S'}(x) := Σ_i|p_{Q(x)}e_i − p_{S'}e_i|² and J(S') := ∫⁻_B ofReal(τ_{S'}(x)) dμ.
0. Measurability. For every subspace S', x ↦ τ_{S'}(x) is μ-a.e. measurable. Case 1: J(T) ≤ ofReal(a). Put S := T. Then S = T, J(S) ≤ ofReal(a) by the case assumption and J(S) ≤ J(T) trivially. It remains to prove the height bound.
1. By sibling proj_algebra (Submission.dorag_tes_projection_algebra), part (b), applied with the triple (Q(x), T, T₁), for every x: c₀ ≤ 2τ_T(x) + 2τ_{T₁}(x), where c₀ := Σ_i|p_Te_i − p_{T₁}e_i|² ≥ 0 is a constant.

Source: parent proof Steps 3–6 (Simon Ch. 5, proof of 4.5, (5)–(16)). This is the combination of (12′) and (13′) with the area-formula transfer. The parent applies it with r := σ/4, e := I := ∫_{B_σ(ξ)}|p_x − p_{T′}|² dμ, a := C₇I and m := 2ω_n(σ/4)ⁿ. Notation: D := B̆ⁿ_{r/2}(0), Φ(v) := ξ + ιv + ι'f(v), F := Φ(ℝⁿ), fʲ := EuclideanSpace.proj j ∘ f, Dg := fderiv ℝ g, ∂_ig(v) := Dg(v)e_i, tilt_T(x) := Σ_i|p_xe_i − p_Te_i|². The sibling contract graph_transfer (b) bounds |(∫_D g) − (∫_{Φ(D)} g(P(x − ξ)) dμ)|, the difference of two separately computed integrals. Step 6.3 uses exactly this form.
1. Let P : ℝ^{n+k} → ℝⁿ be the adjoint of ι (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint of ι as a continuous linear map). For all u: ⟨P(ιv), u⟩ = ⟨ιv, ιu⟩ = ⟨v, u⟩, since ι is an isometry; so P(ιv) = v. Also ⟨P(ι'w), u⟩ = ⟨ι'w, ιu⟩ = 0, so P(ι'w) = 0. Write φ(x) := P(x − ξ).
2. κ ≥ |H(0)| ≥ 0. Each summand is ≤ the sum, so μ(B_r(ξ) ∖ F) ≤ ofReal(a) and Hⁿ((F ∖ spt μ) ∩ B_r(ξ)) ≤ ofReal(a).
3. All hypotheses of sibling graph_variation (Submission.dorag_tes_graph_first_variation_estimate) hold with this P. All hypotheses of sibling graph_transfer (Submission.dorag_tes_graph_parameter_transfer) hold with this P and this a: the Hⁿ-bound is from step 2, and θ = 1 a.e. and Hⁿ((spt μ ∩ W) ∖ M) = 0 are hypotheses. Apply both.
4. Each fʲ is 1-Lipschitz: |fʲ(v) − fʲ(w)| = |(f(v) − f(w))_j| ≤ |f(v) − f(w)| ≤ |v − w|. So ‖Dfʲ(v)‖ ≤ 1 for every v (norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz; Dfʲ(v) = 0 where fʲ is not differentiable).
5. Proof of (E). Fix j and let g(v) := ‖Dfʲ(v)‖². g is measurable (measurable_fderiv) with 0 ≤ g ≤ 1 (step 4). graph_transfer (a) with G := 1 gives (∫⁻_D ofReal(g)) ≤ (∫⁻_{Φ(D)} ofReal(g(φ(x))) dμ) + ofReal(1·a). The middle integrand ofReal(‖Dfʲ(φ(x))‖²) is exactly the integrand of graph_variation (i), so the middle integral is ≤ 2∫⁻_{B_r(ξ)} ofReal(tilt_T) dμ ≤ 2ofReal(e). Hence ∫⁻_D ofReal(g) ≤ 2ofReal(e) + ofReal(a) = ofReal(2e + a), as e, a ≥ 0. Since g ≥ 0 is measurable, ∫_D g = (∫⁻_D ofReal(g)).toReal (integral_eq_lintegral_of_nonneg_ae), which is ≤ 2e + a (ENNReal.toReal_le_of_le_ofReal).
6. Proof of (W). Fix j, ζ and G as stated; G ≥ ‖Dζ(0)‖ ≥ 0. Let g_j(v) := Σ_i ∂_ifʲ(v)∂_iζ(v).
6.1 g_j is measurable (measurable_fderiv_apply_const for both factors). For functionals A, B on ℝⁿ with Riesz vectors a, b (A(x) = ⟨a, x⟩, B(x) = ⟨b, x⟩, ‖A‖ = |a|, ‖B‖ = |b|), Σ_iA(e_i)B(e_i) = Σ_ia_ib_i = ⟨a, b⟩. So |Σ_iA(e_i)B(e_i)| ≤ ‖A‖‖B‖ by Cauchy–Schwarz. Hence |g_j(v)| ≤ ‖Dfʲ(v)‖‖Dζ(v)‖ ≤ 1·G = G.
6.2 For each j′, ‖Df^{j′}‖² is measurable and bounded by 1, and D has finite Lebesgue measure. So it is integrable on D, and by linearity and (E), ∫_D Σ_{j′}‖Df^{j′}‖² = Σ_{j′}∫_D‖Df^{j′}‖² ≤ k(2e + a).
6.3 graph_transfer (b) with g := g_j and this G bounds the absolute value of the difference of the two separately computed integrals: |(∫_D g_j) − (∫_{Φ(D)} g_j(φ(x)) dμ)| ≤ G(a + 2ⁿ(∫_D Σ_{j′}‖Df^{j′}‖²)) ≤ G(a + 2ⁿk(2e + a)), by 6.2 and G ≥ 0.
6.4 The function x ↦ g_j(φ(x)) is exactly the integrand of graph_variation (ii). Combine (ii) with the hypotheses ∫⁻_{B_r(ξ)} ofReal(tilt_T) dμ ≤ ofReal(e), μ(B_r(ξ) ∖ F) ≤ ofReal(a) (step 2) and μ(B_r(ξ)) ≤ ofReal(m). Using G, e, a, m, κr/2 ≥ 0, this gives ofReal|∫_{Φ(D)} g_j(φ(x)) dμ| ≤ ofReal(G)(ofReal(e) + ofReal(a) + ofReal(κr/2)ofReal(m)) = ofReal(G(e + a + κrm/2)). The right-hand real number is ≥ 0, so |∫_{Φ(D)} g_j(φ(x)) dμ| ≤ G(e + a + κrm/2).
6.5 Write X := ∫_D g_j and Y := ∫_{Φ(D)} g_j∘φ dμ. Then |X| = |(X − Y) + Y| ≤ |X − Y| + |Y| ≤ G(a + 2ⁿk(2e + a)) + G(e + a + κrm/2) = G((1 + 2^{n+1}k)e + (2 + 2ⁿk)a + κrm/2). This is ≤ G((2 + 2^{n+1}k)(e + a) + κrm), because the difference equals G(e + 2ⁿka + κrm/2) ≥ 0. This is (W). ∎
